sb_prompt: THE TOPIC IS CLOTHING.  PLEASE FIND OUT HOW THE OTHER CALLER TYPICALLY DRESSES FOR WORK.  HOW MUCH VARIATION IS THERE FROM DAY TO DAY?  HOW MUCH VARIATION IS THERE FROM SEASON TO SEASON?
turns: Yeah, I'm definitely one of those who just can't dress up for a factory floor, I usually just throw on my uniform and sneakers and that's it, no variation at all really.

Oh wow, that is totally different from my life; I get asked to wear scrubs but I still like to swap them out depending on the season, plus my mom wears different shoes every single day just because she can.
Yeah, my sneakers are definitely a no-go; I got hurt last month wearing them and now I'm stuck in these heavy, non-slip boots that don't change color or anything.
That is crazy, I wish I could be stuck in one pair but my mom wouldn't have it; she's got like four pairs of loafers and rotates them weekly to keep her feet happy.
Yeah, four pairs sounds like a lot of work, but at least you can change things up.
Yeah, it's just annoying to coordinate shoes with my scrubs anyway since they're not even color-coded.
Yeah, honestly my whole uniform is faded blue so I don't even care about matching anything, just gotta keep the boots clean.
Yeah, my scrubs are always white so it's actually easier, though I do have a few different colored cardigans for summer versus winter.
Yeah, winter basically just means grabbing my fleece vest over the uniform and that's about it.
Yeah, honestly I just toss the vest on and hope the days don't get too cold, it's kinda nice to know I have options even if I don't use them much.
Yeah, usually I just put on a cheap wool jacket if it dips below freezing.
Yeah, that cheap wool thing sounds about right, honestly I'd rather just freeze a little bit than worry about looking weird.
Yeah, well I guess I'm stuck with it anyway since the company won't pay for anything nicer.
Yeah, I'm kinda the same way about the scrubs; I'd rather just stick with what works than spend hours trying to match a whole new wardrobe.
Yeah, at least you've got the choice to mix it up though, I'd never know what to wear if I wasn't stuck with this exact faded blue thing.
Yeah, but at least I don't have to worry about OSHA fines if someone slips on my old loafers.
Yeah, that's actually a good point, but my boots are so heavy that if I slipped once more, the plant manager would probably write me up again.
Yeah, heavy boots are scary, honestly I'd rather wear something light than risk getting sent home.
Yeah, honestly I'd rather slip and get a ticket than try to justify wearing flimsy sneakers around heavy machinery.
Yeah, I guess comfort is the only thing that really matters in the end.
Yeah, I guess you're right, we both just want to get through the day without getting hurt.
Yeah, for sure, I just won't risk it.
Yeah, it's funny 'cause my cousin works in dentistry too and she literally lost a toe last year just because she wore those cute new flats to the clinic.
Oh wow, that is scary, did she really lose a toe?
Yeah, she actually had to wear the work boots home afterwards because the clinic mandated it, which made the whole thing just so much worse.
That is absolutely terrifying, did she have to walk like that?
Yeah, she couldn't even wear them to the car, just had to shuffle home barefoot until she could get some shoes.
That sounds just awful, how long did she have to do that before she could get back in her shoes?
Yeah, about a week, then they let her go back to sneakers, but she said she still limps every time it rains.
Yeah, that is just the worst, I'm glad she's finally back to normal.
Yeah, honestly I feel bad for her though, I still see her walking a little stiff every now and then.
Yeah, that is just awful, I hope she finally got some good support so it doesn't stay like that forever.
Yeah, I think once her foot heals up enough she'll probably just get custom orthotics instead of going back to those flat shoes.
Yeah, custom insoles sound like the smart move, definitely better than risking another accident.
Yeah, orthotics is probably the only way she's going to walk straight again.
Yeah, that's probably the best long-term fix though.
Yeah, that's probably the smartest thing she could have done.
Yeah, I'll bet that was the best call she made for sure.
Yeah, once she's got those fitted, she'll probably be fine, I've got a cousin who had a broken rib from a spill too so he never wears shoes around the press area again.
Yeah, good riddance to him, I'm glad he's safe from that kind of injury now.
